concerns.text: Task T010 (small‑scale benchmark) consumes the router output produced by T011, yet T010 is listed before T011. This creates a consumer‑before‑producer ordering violation.

Task T004 is tagged `[P]` but writes `data/processed/generation_log.json`, which is later mutated by T005 and T011. The shared file introduces an implicit ordering requirement, so T004 is not parallel‑safe.
Task T005 is tagged `[P]` yet updates the same `generation_log.json` produced by T004 and later modified by T011. This hidden shared state violates the parallel‑safety guarantee.
Task T010 is marked `[P]` but writes `execution_logs.csv` while depending on the router’s `sut_plan` added by T011. The implicit ordering makes T010 not parallel‑safe.

Task T011 is tagged `[P]` yet mutates `generation_log.json` after it has been created by T004 and enriched by T005. This shared‑state mutation requires a strict sequence, so T011 is not parallel‑safe.
